keyFindings.description: The new INFO line `<cache> first watch ended because a rewatch replaced it` gives the wrong cause. watch(w.first, nil, 0) returns an error only before it installs a watcher (bus.ReadStreamState at :513-516, or open with from == 0 at :524-528); with replacing == 0 a replacement never makes it fail. The watch failed on its own (the `error` attribute is the cause, e.g. `nats: connection closed`); a rewatch had only already taken over. Reword it to say that, for example `<cache> first watch failed after a rewatch replaced it; the replacement feeds the cache`, change the `replaced` constant at kvwatch_test.go:189 with it, and fix Start's doc at :191 (`while it is still the live one`: the first watch was never installed, so the condition is `while no watcher is current`, :206). Code and its test change, so it goes through the tester.

The freeze-and-wait-for-both-cut-lines sequence is written twice in two new test files of this pull request: cut_rewatch_test.go:43-65 repeats silent_cut_test.go:42-79 (testnats.Start, startListenerProcess with liveLaneEnv, waitHealthy, the log offset, server.Freeze with t.Cleanup(thaw), the loop on disconnectedUnderName for both client names under silentCutBound). Extract one helper in silent_cut_test.go (for example `freezeUntilBothClientsReportTheCut(t, server, listener) (thaw func(), output func() string)`, keeping the per-client missing diagnostic and the timing log) and call it from both tests, so a fix to the wait lands once.
